evidence: CancelOrderUseCase.execute returns an inline literal { id: order.id, status: order.getStatus(), lines: order.lines, createdAt: order.createdAt.toISOString() }
ListOrdersByStatusUseCase.execute builds the same OrderDto literal inside orders.map
UpdateOrderStatusUseCase.execute builds the same OrderDto literal inline
PlaceOrderUseCase has private mapToDto(order: Order): OrderDto with the same mapping, not shared with the other use cases
UpdateOrderStatusUseCase.execute hardcodes validStatuses: OrderStatus[] = ['placed','paid','packed','shipped','delivered'] after casting request.status as OrderStatus
PlaceOrderUseCase.execute calls orderRepository.save(order), but UpdateOrderStatusUseCase (order.transitionTo) and CancelOrderUseCase (stockManager.releaseStock) change state without calling save
PlaceOrderUseCase.execute checks Order invariants itself ('Order must contain at least one line', quantity <= 0) instead of leaving them to the Order entity
parsedVerdict.reasoning: The use cases do serve one concern (order and stock handling), but the same rules are copied across files. The Order-to-OrderDto mapping is written out separately in four use cases, and only PlaceOrderUseCase has it as a private mapToDto that the others don't reuse. UpdateOrderStatusUseCase hardcodes the list of valid OrderStatus values, which belongs with the domain status type and Order.transitionTo. Repository use is also inconsistent: PlaceOrder saves the order after changing it, while UpdateOrderStatus and CancelOrder change orders without calling save. CancelOrder also releases stock without moving the order to a cancelled status.

violations.message: execute() copies the Order-to-OrderDto mapping inline instead of using a shared mapper. It releases stock without moving the order to a cancelled status or saving it.

private mapToDto() is a fourth copy of the Order-to-OrderDto mapping and isn't shared. execute() also checks Order invariants (non-empty lines, positive quantity) itself instead of leaving them to the Order entity.

execute() hardcodes the list of valid OrderStatus values, which belongs with the domain status type and Order.transitionTo. It copies the OrderDto mapping inline and changes the order without saving it, unlike PlaceOrderUseCase.
